title: Meet Dollfication: Community Choice Award Winner of Creator's Contest 2025 Vol. 2 TOKYO CONTINUUM!
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/7d219e29b31941549b062b6a6a85949a/images/4830561374eb498eb2c23b250c590c6bjc07.png)_Introducing our interview with_[ _Dollfication_](https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/d6079ef4604240bc85f41958bf578fd3) _, Community Choice Award winner of TOKYO CONTINUUM! ✨_

##  _Discover how she visioned her "Tokyo Continuum" in a doll - an aesthetics blend of anime, sci-fi, and a playful yet confident theme of pink._

![f9fe28a2bf3a44f89a123b3728ca4e33](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/7d219e29b31941549b062b6a6a85949a/images/f9fe28a2bf3a44f89a123b3728ca4e33jc07.png)

# **Artist Introduction: please tell us about yourself.**

Hello! My name is Dollfication, and I’m currently a fashion design student specializing primarily in doll and toy design.

I decided to join this contest because of my deep fascination with Japanese fashion and trends. Japan has such a unique and bold fashion culture that constantly pushes boundaries, and I’m inspired by how it blends art, design, and storytelling. Participating in this contest gives me a chance to immerse myself more in these influences and apply them to my own creative process.

In addition to traditional design, I also work with 3D programs like Marvelous Designer and Blender to create digital models of my designs. These tools allow me to bring my concepts to life in a virtual space, which is an exciting way to explore different garment structures and textures before physically creating them. Perfect for me as a doll/toy designer.

* * *

# **We’d like to hear more about the art direction in your Creator’s contest 2025 Vol.2.**  
**What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

For my submission to the Creator’s Contest 2025 Vol. 2, I drew inspiration from anime aesthetics, sci-fi, and a touch of gyaru fashion, with a focus on a doll-like aesthetic. My main goal was to create a futuristic, metallic look using sharp lines and dynamic silhouettes, while keeping everything centered around one color: pink.

![7d5ba1e2d1034d26a403065a1daa920a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/7d219e29b31941549b062b6a6a85949a/images/7d5ba1e2d1034d26a403065a1daa920ahhh6.png)

Pink was chosen for its versatility—it’s playful yet bold, which worked perfectly with the sci-fi, anime, and doll-like influences. The minimal use of gyaru fashion added an element of confidence and attitude. Overall, I aimed for a striking balance between strength, simplicity, elegance, and fantasy, with pink unifying the design.

* * *

# **Would you be able to give us a quick overview of the different tools you use in your pipeline with a focus on Marvelous Designer?**  
**Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

In my workflow, I primarily used Marvelous Designer to create the outfit for my design. The process was smooth and straightforward, as I had a clear vision from the start. I didn’t encounter any major difficulties, and the program’s intuitive tools allowed me to focus on execution rather than troubleshooting.

![e8a56ef68b4e437f98eac029fccfd075](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/7d219e29b31941549b062b6a6a85949a/images/e8a56ef68b4e437f98eac029fccfd075bandicam%202025-08-12%2016-25-43-982.jpg)

The first step was importing the basic measurements for my avatar, which gave me a realistic base for designing the garments. I began by sketching out the patterns for each piece of the outfit in Marvelous Designer, paying close attention to the futuristic, metallic look I wanted to achieve. The program’s pattern drafting tools allowed me to create precise shapes and experiment with different cuts and details, which was crucial for achieving the clean, structured look I had in mind.

![54a7d22f70894b168b51251ea7e55b9b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/7d219e29b31941549b062b6a6a85949a/images/54a7d22f70894b168b51251ea7e55b9bbandicam%202025-08-12%2016-32-03-947.jpg)

Once the basic patterns were laid out, I used the simulation feature to see how the fabrics would move and react in real time. This feature helped me fine-tune the fit and flow of the garments, ensuring that everything appeared natural on the avatar. I also made use of the fabric library to select materials that matched the metallic and holographic look I was aiming for, adjusting the properties such as weight and stiffness to get the right texture. Once the outfit was complete, I adjusted the colors and added subtle finishing touches to match my overall aesthetic.

* * *

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

![b665e993e77c42f7ab286e8e91b5198a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/7d219e29b31941549b062b6a6a85949a/images/b665e993e77c42f7ab286e8e91b5198abandicam%202025-08-12%2016-31-37-104.jpg)

One tip I’d share is to use the simulation feature early and often. It helps you see how fabrics behave on the avatar in real-time, which makes it easier to adjust fit and flow without any guesswork. Layering fabrics is another great trick. By combining materials with different properties, you can create depth and texture, especially for metallic or holographic effects. Make use of Avatar Collisions to ensure your garment fits properly, especially in tight or complex designs. It prevents weird bulges or misalignments. Also, if you’re working with multiple pieces, use the "Arrange All" tool to organize your patterns before sewing them together. It saves time and keeps things neat. Lastly, always use the Sewing Simulation to check for any issues with seam placement or overlaps before finalizing the design. These tips can help streamline your process and make the most of Marvelous Designer’s features.
content_description: Explore our interview with Dollfication, the Community Choice Award winner of TOKYO CONTINUUM, as she shares her creative journey and insights into her innovative doll design inspired by anime, sci-fi, and bold pink aesthetics.

title: Interview with Kimia Bagherzadeh Homaei, Winner of Creator's Contest 2025 Vol. 2 TOKYO CONTINUUM
content:
## _Introducing our exclusive interview with_[ _Kimia Bagherzadeh Homaei_](https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/19ad7f6438eb4c849a69b703ce0f8c3a) _, winner of TOKYO CONTINUUM! ✨_

##  _Her "Tokyo Continuum" collection tells the story of Japan's fox and deer spirits, brought to life through a beautiful collision of architecture, technology, and fashion._

![90eb738e85534984a259f65a80a062b0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/90eb738e85534984a259f65a80a062b079101535deb044a59920066919f4d02a51-2.jpg)

# **Artist Introduction: please tell us about yourself.**

Hello everyone! I'm Kimia, a digital fashion designer from Iran with an architect's eye for structure and a storyteller's heart. When I first discovered Marvelous Designer two years ago, it felt like finding the perfect creative partner - one that understood my need for both precision and poetry in design.

![07d02870ab0742f692eae207a1a3d861](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/07d02870ab0742f692eae207a1a3d861Introduction-Interior-Design-Collage.jpg)

My architectural background gives me a unique perspective. Where some see just fabric and seams, I see tension points and load-bearing curves. Marvelous Designer became my bridge between worlds, letting me apply architectural principles to flowing garments while still keeping that magical sense of movement and life. I've had particular fun connecting it to Rhino and Grasshopper - there's something thrilling about seeing parametric patterns transform into wearable art, then adding that final touch of personality through EveryWear's animations.

![9311e87518cc48c28f84815bc30a6f98](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/9311e87518cc48c28f84815bc30a6f98Introduction-Computational-Design-Collage.jpg)

**Why This Contest Called to Me >>>**

I entered because I wanted to prove fashion could be more than clothing - it could be wearable mythology. My "Tokyo Continuum" collection tells the story of Japan's fox and deer spirits through every intentional wrinkle and fold. The origami-like structures? That's my architectural side speaking. The way the fabrics flow and interact? That's where Marvelous Designer's magic shines.

**What This Journey Taught Me >>>**

  1. The most compelling designs live in the tension between opposites - structure and fluidity, tradition and innovation

  2. Technical tools (like my beloved Rhino integrations) work best when they serve the story, not the other way around

  3. There's incredible power in garments that don't just cover bodies, but spark imaginations




Winning has been humbling, but what excites me most is knowing this is just the beginning. I can't wait to keep exploring how many other stories might come to life through this beautiful collision of architecture, technology and fashion.

# **We’d like to hear more about the art direction in your Creator’s contest 2025 Vol.2. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

For this contest, I envisioned a theatrical fashion moment where ancient Japanese folklore collides with contemporary street style - a visual dialogue between tradition and rebellion. At its heart lies the dance between two mythical spirits: the cunning Kitsune (fox) and graceful Shika (deer), reimagined through a modern fashion lens that celebrates their contradictions.

![33b56f79a7a743878854ff8d34ba3d98](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/33b56f79a7a743878854ff8d34ba3d98Concept-Elements-Collage.jpg)

The Fox Character (Kitsune) >>> became a study in deceptive beauty:

  1. Sharp, defensive poses with angular body language

  2. A fiery red-and-white ensemble featuring:



  * Razor-sharp stiletto heels with peony motifs carved into their surfaces

  * Nine trailing fabric strips representing the fox's mythical tails

  * Origami-like folded elements creating aggressive silhouettes



  3. Metallic gold kintsugi seams highlighting intentional "flaws"

![0a216f223fef4fce8fd0e9ebd02b0683](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/0a216f223fef4fce8fd0e9ebd02b0683Fox.png)![d6bc9dbb4f3b4d8eb139b0bfb1d4e415](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/d6bc9dbb4f3b4d8eb139b0bfb1d4e415Fox-Character-collage.jpg)




The Deer Spirit (Shika) >>> embodies vulnerable strength:

  1. Softer but assertive stances contrasting the fox's angles

  2. An ethereal white-and-green palette with:



  * Delicate, translucent fabrics veiling the face

  * A single glowing tear emphasizing hidden purity

  * Hoof-like platform shoes with curved, organic shapes

  * Floral embroidery rooted in natural motifs




![1998ad2e237b4740bd47b46fc11b93a6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/1998ad2e237b4740bd47b46fc11b93a6Deer.png)![40fa0c593e1145858827b1b5dd596185](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/40fa0c593e1145858827b1b5dd596185Deer-Character-collage.jpg)

Their Shared Stage >>> blends these opposing energies:

  1. The forest emerges through layered textures - bark-like pleats, petal-strewn fabrics

  2. Harajuku influences appear in unexpected places: deconstructed obi sashes, streetwear-inspired layering

  3. Every movement becomes part of their dance - the fox's sharp gestures meeting the deer's fluid motions




![8ae79c343bbb44a88cfa4b1978926925](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/8ae79c343bbb44a88cfa4b1978926925Both.png)![2d895a2445624123895ecbd4cb86aa5f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/2d895a2445624123895ecbd4cb86aa5fBoth-Characters-collage%20%2812%29.jpg)![735743fe3083485f88bfb23462f5c28c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/735743fe3083485f88bfb23462f5c28cBoth-Shoes-Collage.jpg)

This isn't just clothing; it's wearable theater where:

Cultural symbols become contemporary fashion statements, Every design choice reveals character psychology, Traditional crafts (kintsugi/origami) dialogue with digital techniques and Nature and urban aesthetics perform together.

The ultimate visual paradox? Creating harmony from opposition - where the fox's calculated seduction and the deer's quiet strength find balance in motion, proving that the most compelling beauty often lives in tension between opposites.

# **Would you be able to give us a quick overview of the different tools you use in your pipeline with a focus on Marvelous Designer? Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

You know, when I first started this project, I had this vivid image in my mind of how these mythical characters should move and interact through fashion. Bringing that vision to life became this fascinating journey between traditional craftsmanship and digital innovation.

It all began with my sketchbook - there's something irreplaceable about putting pencil to paper when working out initial concepts. Those rough drawings of the fox and deer spirits were my North Star throughout the process. But to really visualize the designs, I turned to AI tools, feeding detailed descriptions into Copilot to generate concept art that captured the mystical quality I was after. [Krea.ai](http://Krea.ai) then helped transform those static images into moving references, which was incredibly helpful for understanding how fabrics might flow.

![18329ed97e61441b8d0ca9f74a794e9e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/9d909f48e90245078561b791b74571ed/images/18329ed97e61441b8d0ca9f74a794e9eCopilot-Ai-Concept-Collage.jpg)

Now, the real magic happened in Marvelous Designer. I remember spending days perfecting the patterns - the fox's angular, origami-inspired elements needed such precise measurements, while the deer's flowing layers required a completely different approach.

The biggest "aha" moment came when working with EveryWear. We had these dramatic pose changes where normally the clothing would go completely wild, but by carefully mapping the bone attachments and creating flexible zones, I managed to keep everything looking natural. It was like teaching the garments how to move with the characters.

For materials and rendering, I lived in CLO3D - must have created about twenty different fabric variations before landing on the perfect ones. Those kintsugi gold seams on the fox's outfit? Each one needed special attention to catch the light just right. And the deer's translucent veil went through so many iterations to get that balance between coverage and delicacy.

The final animations through KLING AI were actually the easiest part, which surprised me! After all that technical work, seeing the characters come to life with their fabrics moving naturally felt like magic. It's funny - what started as separate elements (the sharp fox, the soft deer) ended up feeling like one cohesive dance when everything came together.

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

One of Marvelous Designer's greatest strengths is how beautifully it plays with other software. Here's what I've discovered through experimentation:

**Seamless Parametric Workflow >>>**

Many designers don't realize how well MD integrates with parametric tools. My favorite pipeline:

  1. Generate base patterns in Rhino/Grasshopper

  2. Apply parametric adjustments (like graded sizing or organic curves)

  3. Export as 2D PDF files

  4. Import directly into Marvelous Designer as editable patterns




Yes, there's some cleanup needed (I always check stitch lines and pivot points), but the ability to create algorithmically-generated patterns that still work with MD's physics engine is game-changing. I used this exact method for the origami elements in my contest piece - the precision from Grasshopper combined with MD's natural drape created perfect structured-yet-organic folds.

**EveryWear Pro Tip >>>**

Most people use EveryWear just for stabilization, but it's also fantastic for:

  * Creating "memory" in fabrics (like wrinkled areas that persist through movements)

  * Setting up custom flex zones for mixed-material garments




**Unexpected Uses >>>**

Beyond fashion, I've had success with:

  * Architectural tensile structures

  * Furniture upholstery simulations

  * Even abstract art installations with floating fabrics
content_description: Explore the enchanting world of Kimia Bagherzadeh Homaei's "Tokyo Continuum" collection, where Japanese folklore intertwines with cutting-edge fashion and architecture to create a captivating narrative through wearable art.

title: Auto Fitting tool fitting garments backwards
content:
Hi,

I've been experimenting with the Auto-Fitting / Re-Drape option of Marvelous Designer on my custom avatar. I'm trying to re-drape garments from the store and the garments are fitted backwards.  
  
My custom avatar has a fitting suit and the garment I'm importing also has one![02fbe63eea4141d2899f6475104b4a5d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/5995395acd694cfdb3ffabf003475e79/images/02fbe63eea4141d2899f6475104b4a5dfitting_suit.png)![5a353316ea1c4468a4c8112c932a2357](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/5995395acd694cfdb3ffabf003475e79/images/5a353316ea1c4468a4c8112c932a2357image.png)

When I select the garment and click "Re-drape 3D Arrangement", it is fitted backwards :

![fad1561cd8fa4a249377199c72623024](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/5995395acd694cfdb3ffabf003475e79/images/fad1561cd8fa4a249377199c72623024image.png)![72cfbddf05334faaac3d193520fc415e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/5995395acd694cfdb3ffabf003475e79/images/72cfbddf05334faaac3d193520fc415eimage.png)

Has anyone an idea why this happens ?

Thanks a lot for your help !

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hey! Yes, this is an issue from the last patch, and we are already working on it.It is triggered when manually creating the fitting suit on the Custom Avatars. If you have the option, please try to apply the Autofitting feature when importing the Avatar. For what we tested, the error won't be triggered this way. We will release a hotfix once we resolve this issue.
content_description: This webpage aims to seek assistance and insights on resolving the issue of garments fitting backwards when using the Auto-Fitting/Re-Drape feature in Marvelous Designer with a custom avatar.

title: Fabric Folds Not Realistic Enough? Who You Gonna Call?
content:
## _Unnatural wrinkles are the ghosts that haunt digital garments. To bust them, 3D artist Johnny Xiao became an investigator of realism for his Ghostbusters_ _Spengler_ _project. His secret weapon? Not a proton pack of details, but a sharp eye for what to remove._

* * *

# ![7147926abc334e308dc161a583880b9e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/7147926abc334e308dc161a583880b9ejohnny-xiao-zhiqiang-xiao-11.jpg)**Interview with**[**Johnny Xiao**](https://www.artstation.com/johnnyxiao)**|**[**Ghostbusters Spengler**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/NqmGzd)**| 3D Artist**  


* * *

# **Please introduce yourself to the Marvelous Designer community.**

Hello everyone. I’m Johnny Xiao, a senior 3D artist in the game and film industry.

# **What’s the story behind your work? Why did you decide to recreate Spengler from Ghostbusters?**

I first saw _Ghostbusters_ back in middle school, and it totally stuck with me. I was also super into movies like _Starship Troopers_ , _Back to the Future, and The Fifth Element_. These movies all played a significant role in inspiring me to pursue a career in this industry.

![454e82f2e4014cebba3ddc8836f6a5d0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/454e82f2e4014cebba3ddc8836f6a5d0johnny-xiao-zhiqiang-xiao-12.jpg)

# **As an experienced Marvelous Designer user, did you apply any unconventional techniques or workflows in this project to enhance the realism or efficiency of the garment creation?**

For this project, I mainly followed a traditional workflow. However, I made extensive use of **_internal lines_** to create **_memory creases_** , which significantly enhanced the realism of the clothing. 

I also gathered a lot of references, especially worn garments, to study the subtle details of wrinkling and curling. For example, instead of letting the collar completely droop, I added a slight lift and tension to make it look more natural and lived-in.

![50ae7bafeb85469087b249db24fbb5cb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/50ae7bafeb85469087b249db24fbb5cbjohnny-xiao-zhiqiang-xiao-14.jpg)

![7bef7d3c2adf48c8ad727a509dd6184c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/7bef7d3c2adf48c8ad727a509dd6184cJohnnyXiao6.jpg)

![c0b174ced7874627ae208dd9e7fb23c8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/c0b174ced7874627ae208dd9e7fb23c8JohnnyXiao7.jpg)

![7aea9987240745229199958d6bf710d1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/7aea9987240745229199958d6bf710d1johnnyXiao1.jpg)

![4f55fae2cc9b46e4895bf26e26f09658](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/4f55fae2cc9b46e4895bf26e26f09658JohnnyXiao2.png)

![0c3b3704c5e54feb936c4d3e6ebe64d2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/0c3b3704c5e54feb936c4d3e6ebe64d2Johnnyxiao1.png)

# **What part of the process do you enjoy the most, and what do you find most challenging?**

Whenever I work on a personal project, I aim to make it better than the last. 

The biggest challenge for me is achieving a high level of realism in Marvelous Designer, which requires a great deal of patience and attention to detail. While many artists tend to add more wrinkles to their garments, I believe that **_subtraction is often the key_** —matching folds precisely to real-world references is both the most difficult and the most rewarding part of the process.

![91a61522fc2c47e28b8b0916f9c7759f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/91a61522fc2c47e28b8b0916f9c7759fJohnnyXiao2.jpg)

![f47976a76eef480fb6eba97e39722854](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/f47976a76eef480fb6eba97e39722854johnny-xiao-zhiqiang-xiao-20.jpg)

# **In your opinion, what is Marvelous Designer’s greatest strength in character creation? How did you leverage that in this project?**

In traditional workflows, we often relied on sculpting in ZBrush to achieve realistic clothing, which certainly works well. 

However, **_Marvelous Designer significantly improves production efficiency by allowing for rapid garment modeling and the generation of natural-looking folds_**. These folds can be adjusted in real time and respond dynamically to movement, creating a much more lifelike result. 

In today’s fast-paced production environment, this is a major advantage. With the current speed of GPU-based simulation and improved stability, quick iteration has become much more feasible, enabling the creation of highly realistic assets with greater efficiency.

![084ecda70e524b00b1c271a74e04edc7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/084ecda70e524b00b1c271a74e04edc7JohnnyXiao5.jpg)

![ac559a5aa39342a78ec553347154bc44](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/ac559a5aa39342a78ec553347154bc44johnny-xiao-zhiqiang-xiao-16.jpg)![4d44edb926504a768d511027307b3010](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/4d44edb926504a768d511027307b3010johnny-xiao-zhiqiang-xiao-19.jpg)

# **For artists already familiar with Marvelous Designer, how would you recommend further unlocking its potential in character creation?**

As I mentioned earlier, efficiency is everything today. 

It’s not about working harder, but working smarter—finding ways to produce high-quality results without spending excessive time manually refining every garment. 

Marvelous Designer isn’t a difficult tool to learn, though many are initially discouraged by the pattern-making process. Fortunately, there’s now a wealth of free online assets available. For example, **_the CONNECT store offers a wide range of free assets_**. You can modify these to suit your character, allowing you to quickly create high-quality models with minimal effort.

![fa8379b9afa44674a14ea27084941f4f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/82276b26a47540da8e2d60799e041cc1/images/fa8379b9afa44674a14ea27084941f4fCONNECT%20store.png)

title: Solved: Clo/MD LineSync and Z Position in Unreal
content:
Hello, I'm new to Marvelous Designer and have followed many tutorials but I'm having an issue that I cannot seem to find a solution to - so I am here asking for help.  
  
Note: I am using Unreal Engine 5.6, Metahuman 5.6, CLO/MD LiveSync, MD Version 2025.1.107  
  
I was able to get my Metahuman into Marvelous Designer, add a garment from the library, and fit the garment to my Metahuman in MD.   
  
When I "Update"/Sync MD in UE the garment Z position is off and thus does not align with may MH skeleton - See Pics.  
  
In the pic with the long black skirt, I had to reposition everything in the +Z direction and lengthen the skirt to meet the floor. As you can see in the pic the bottom of the garment is at the floor but everything else areas to be moved upward - about the amount I had to lengthen the skirt?  
  
In the pick with the white dress with its skeleton, I did not alter this garment in MD, I simply used the simulation to fit it to my MH avatar. You can see the garment is incorrectly positioned int e Z direction.  
  
What could I be doing wrong? Thanks for any help you can provide.  
  
Update: Last image in UE is the Black Skirt and top unedited but repositioned to fit my MH avatar.  
  
Update 2: As I investigate this, I have noticed a 4" discrepancy in the heights between my Metahuman and the imported Avatar in MD. My metahuman is 68" tall and the Avatar is 72" tall. Not sure if this is the problem as the garment appears to be off greater than this 4" discrepancy - it's closer to 6".  
  
![a01a0e3320dd4ba395a062a8a7c93c14](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/8def7553a9e1486cb7e271485f0c216e/images/a01a0e3320dd4ba395a062a8a7c93c14Screenshot%202025-09-02%20093250.png)![d32c7642abb142e29e64ec175cd3e8b9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/8def7553a9e1486cb7e271485f0c216e/images/d32c7642abb142e29e64ec175cd3e8b9Screenshot%202025-09-02%20093741.png)![4c31aad76bbf441595ec858c13e5b73d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/8def7553a9e1486cb7e271485f0c216e/images/4c31aad76bbf441595ec858c13e5b73dScreenshot%202025-09-02%20110315.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: The previously described discrepancy was the culprit! I recreated the animation pose asset and resynced the Skeletal Mesh and this fixed the issue.

Comment 2: As I investigate this, I have noticed a 4" discrepancy in the heights between my Metahuman and the imported Avatar in MD. My metahuman is 68" tall and the Avatar is 72" tall. Not sure if this is the problem as the garment appears to be off greater than this 4" discrepancy - it's closer to 6". The attached screenshot shows the discrepancy between the Skeletal Mesh that was created for use to create the Animation Sequence to use in LiveSync.
content_description: This webpage serves as a support forum for users encountering alignment issues between garments in Marvelous Designer and Metahuman avatars within Unreal Engine, seeking solutions and community assistance.
